summary: Deschutes NF lookout on a volcanic cone: L-4 cab built 1933 after a 1932 designation, abandoned 1952; registers say it is now gone, with no site description found.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a volcanic cone
facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1952; the register and firelookout.com say it is now gone
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Deschutes National Forest

events.note: Designated a fire lookout station by the Deschutes National Forest; Arthur Estes to man it (announcement only; no source confirms he did)
A five-mile telephone line was planned to reach the butte
L-4 cab; the register and firelookout.com both give 1933
CCC carpentry crew from the Odell Lake camp completed a garage in September, per the lookout history
Horse Ridge fire, a mile long, origin undetermined, discovered by the Fuzztail Butte lookout (August 1939)

evidence.supports: built in 1933 on a volcano cone, L-4 cab, abandoned 1952, now gone
evidence.quote: Built in 1933 on a volcano cone, this L-4 cab was abandoned in 1952 and is now gone.
1932: A five mile telephone line to be constructed to Fuzztail Butte.

evidence.supports: 1932 designation as lookout station, Fort Rock district, Arthur Estes to man it
evidence.quote: Fuzztail butte, in the Fort Rock district, near Swamp Wells, has been designated by the Deschutes national forest as a fireman-lookout station and will be manned in the near future by Arthur Estes.

evidence.supports: 1934 CCC carpentry crew from Odell Lake completed a garage in September
evidence.quote: 1934: The carpentry crew from the CCC camp at Odell Lake completed the construction of a garage in September.

evidence.supports: August 1939 Horse Ridge fire of undetermined origin
evidence.quote: Horse Ridge was the scene of a mile-long fire of undetermined origin which broke out at noon today.

evidence.supports: fire discovered by the Fuzztail Butte lookout, just east of the station
evidence.quote: Located by the Fuzztail Butte lookout, the timber blaze was discovered just east of this station

evidence.supports: 38 CCC men from Elk Lake and Pringle Falls worked the fire from the west edge
evidence.quote: Thirty-eight CCC men from Elk Lake and Pringle Falls were attaching from the west edge of the fire

evidence.supports: the lookout history ends with a single entry, Removed, no date

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com agree on 1933. The 1932 newspaper item describes a planned station, so it is reported as a designation, not a build date.

notes_for_editor: Bend Bulletin item is read from the Rex's Fire Lookout Page transcription; the original paper was not checked. The Removed entry on the lookout history has no date, so no removal event is recorded. A 1991 Forest Service eligibility study of Deschutes National Forest lookouts is listed in Oregon's digital collections (https://digitalcollections.library.oregon.gov/nodes/view/275303); it was not read and may describe the site. Access level not set: no source says whether the site is open. Staffing: only the 1932 plan is recorded. No photo URLs with credits were found.
